name: Virginia Gardens Village Council

meetings.pattern: Once a month on the third Thursday (with exceptions), 5:30 p.m. in 2026, Village Hall, 6498 NW 38th Terrace, Virginia Gardens, FL 33166. No regular meeting in December; the July and August 2026 regular meetings were cancelled. The pattern is read from the 2026 meeting table, not a written rule.

schedule.note: Council Meeting, 5:30 to 6:30 p.m.; agenda not yet posted

phases.name: Budget workshop
phases.decides: Overview of the 2026/2027 budget worksheets with the council, 5:30 p.m.

phases.name: First budget hearing
phases.decides: Tentative millage and tentative FY 2026/27 budget. Time not readable: the agenda PDF is a scan without text.

phases.name: Final budget meeting
phases.decides: Final millage and FY 2026/27 budget, held with a special council meeting the same evening. Time not readable from the scanned agenda.

phases.name: Fiscal year begins
phases.decides: The village labels its budget 'Fiscal Year 2026/2027'; the October 1 start is the Florida municipal standard and was not stated on a readable village page.

phases.name: Candidate qualifying for the November 3, 2026 election
phases.decides: Who is on the ballot for Mayor and three council seats; 9 a.m. Wednesday July 22 through 5 p.m. Friday August 21, 2026, filed with the Village Clerk.

phases.name: Village general election
phases.decides: Mayor (two-year term) and three council seats (the two highest vote-getters get four-year terms, the third a two-year term); polls 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Candidates: Mayor Tim Boylan and Fred Spencer Deno IV; Council Jorge Arce, Elizabeth Taylor-Martinez, Michael Tur.

levers.how: Speak during the Citizen Comments item at the monthly council meeting at Village Hall.
levers.rules: Time limit and sign-up rule not found: the 2026 agenda PDFs are scans with no readable text and the village posts no rules of procedure online. Minutes show a standing 'Citizen Comments' item.

levers.how: No written comment procedure is published. Email the Village Clerk, Maritza Fernandez-Guevara, at Mfernandez@virginiagardens-fl.gov or the mayor at mayor@virginiagardens-fl.gov.

Email the mayor at mayor@virginiagardens-fl.gov or a council member at first initial plus last name at virginiagardens-fl.gov (for example dconover@virginiagardens-fl.gov), or call Village Hall at 305-871-6104.
Ask the Village Clerk, who fulfills public records requests, at Mfernandez@virginiagardens-fl.gov or 305-871-6104.

Charter amendment by petition is available under state law: a petition signed by 10 percent of the registered electors as of the last municipal general election forces a referendum at the next general election or a special election.
levers.rules: Fla. Stat. 166.031(1). The village charter is not posted on the village site and no online code library copy was found, so any charter initiative section is not recorded.

levers.how: Not found. The charter was not readable (see petition); only the state charter-amendment referendum route under Fla. Stat. 166.031 is confirmed.

Recall follows Florida's uniform municipal recall statute, which applies to every city whether or not its charter has a recall section. For a village with 500 to 1,999 registered electors the first petition needs the greater of 100 electors or 10 percent, gathered within 30 days; for fewer than 500, the greater of 50 or 10 percent. A second 'Recall Petition and Defense' round needs 15 percent within 60 days.
levers.rules: Fla. Stat. 100.361(1), (2)(b), (2)(f), (3)(a), (3)(c), (11), (12). File with the Village Clerk. Elector count not checked; pick the tier from county registration figures.
levers.deadline: 30 days for the first round; 60 days for the second

levers.how: File qualifying papers with the Village Clerk during the window (2026: 9 a.m. July 22 to 5 p.m. August 21). Fees: Mayor $50 plus $210.36 state assessment; Council $25 plus $66.54. Must be a qualified Miami-Dade elector and a village resident for at least three years before qualifying.
levers.rules: From the clerk's 2026 Candidate Qualifying Information and fee notice; no charter section cited.
levers.deadline: 5 p.m. on the last day of qualifying

levers.how: Vote November 3, 2026, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., for Mayor and up to three council members.
levers.rules: Registered voters living in the village.

levers.how: No advisory boards or application page were found on the village site; the village recruits poll workers for its elections through a sign-up form.

elections.terms: Elections every two years. Mayor serves a two-year term. Three council seats are filled each election: the two highest vote-getters get four-year terms, the third a two-year term; the top vote-getter is council president for two years. Elections moved from September (2017, 2021 ballots) to November (2024, 2026).
